_about: Flagged for Review. Types: 'irregularity' (something in the repo, API or docs that looks wrong or inconsistent), 'unverified' (a value or claim that could not be confirmed from an official source; left blank or marked), 'decision' (a choice made by the agent that the owner should confirm), 'blocker' (work that cannot finish without something only the owner can provide). Flags never block the merge; they are published here so the owner can review and request changes.

flags.title: Market status words differ between the filter and the response
flags.detail: The GET /markets status filter uses unopened / open / paused / closed / settled, but the Market.status field in responses uses initialized / inactive / active / closed / determined / disputed / amended / finalized. The dashboard treats status 'active' as tradable (the response value). Confirm this mapping with Kalshi before relying on status filters.

flags.title: Fee rounding wording vs. the fee table
flags.detail: The fee schedule says 'round up such that the fee + positionCost is rounded to a centicent', but every table value is a whole-cent amount. The code rounds the fee up to the whole cent. All 21 General Trading Fees Table rows (1-contract and 100-contract columns) match, and the test passes. Ask Kalshi to confirm the rounding rule for fractional-cent positions.

flags.title: Fee schedule PDF text layer is scrambled in parts
flags.detail: The Non-Standard Fees table (MLB, NCAA, NFL, NBA and other series pages) is garbled in the extracted text (for example overlapping titles such as 'WRoeoskteiernof'). The dashboard does not hard-code those multipliers. It reads fee_type and fee_multiplier for each series from the live API. A human should open the PDF and compare any series used for trading.

flags.title: SDK package metadata has placeholders
flags.detail: The kalshi-typescript npm metadata lists repository and homepage as https://github.com/GIT_USER_ID/GIT_REPO_ID, which are unfilled template placeholders. The package is published by a maintainer named 'kalshi' (npm metadata), so the publisher is plausibly Kalshi, but the source repository could not be confirmed from the package metadata.

flags.title: SDK default base URL is production, not demo
flags.detail: The official SDK's default BASE_PATH is https://external-api.kalshi.com/trade-api/v2 (production). Code copied from SDK examples without a base override calls production, while the project brief names demo hosts. Keys are environment-specific (S3, S6).

flags.title: Rate limit for unauthenticated public requests is not stated
flags.detail: The rate-limit page says unauthenticated requests have separate limits and to back off on 429, but gives no number. The collector limits itself to about 7 requests per second, retries on 429/5xx with backoff, and runs about every 15 minutes. Its real headroom is unverified.

flags.title: Market data comes from PRODUCTION, not the demo host
flags.detail: The brief asks to track live events on Kalshi, and public market-data endpoints need no key. The dashboard reads production public data from external-api.kalshi.com. Demo prices 'may not be reflective of those in real markets' (S4). Set the KALSHI_BASE secret/variable to https://external-api.demo.kalshi.co/trade-api/v2 to switch the dashboard to demo data. Please confirm which you want.

flags.title: Demo-account portfolio and trade execution are NOT connected
flags.detail: Reading the demo account and placing demo orders need a demo API key pair created in Kalshi account settings. Those keys were not provided and cannot be created from this session, so no balance, positions or orders are shown, and no orders have been placed. Add repository secrets KALSHI_DEMO_KEY_ID and KALSHI_DEMO_PRIVATE_KEY to enable the portfolio view. The signing code follows the official spec (S6) and is tested offline.

flags.title: Second-level price ticks need a streaming server
flags.detail: The site refreshes about every 15 minutes through a scheduled collector, so the time axis can show minutes and hours but not seconds. The WebSocket API requires an API key (S8), and GitHub Pages is static, so true per-second charts need a small always-on service that holds the key. This is a suggestion on the Suggestions page, not built here.

flags.title: Cause links for ≥ $0.10 moves are NOT determined
flags.detail: The brief asks for news or website links that may have caused each sharp move. Nothing in the Kalshi API identifies a cause, and no news source was connected. Alerts carry the official market and rules links only, marked 'cause link: not determined'. Adding causes would need manual review.

links.label: Market detail endpoint (source of each alert)

flags.title: Settlement sources and resolution rules are shown as published by Kalshi, not checked
flags.detail: Each series' settlement_sources, contract_url and contract_terms_url are displayed as returned by the API. The gas series (KXAAAGASM) settlement source in particular was not read; check its published rules before trading on it.

links.label: Kalshi Fee Schedule (PDF), KXAAAGASM 'US gas price' row

flags.title: 'Est. 24h $ volume' is a derived estimate, not an official Kalshi dollar figure
flags.detail: Computed as volume_24h_fp × notional_value_dollars, both official fields. The formula is ours and is labeled 'derived' on each page.

flags.title: 'High-ROI' is a placeholder rule, not your model
flags.detail: No model was provided. The dashboard uses a transparent rule (entry ≤ 40¢, spread ≤ 5¢, 24h volume ≥ 100 contracts) defined in config/topics.json. Replace it with your model's outputs when available. The rule is not a prediction and makes no claim about profitability.

flags.title: Topic series list is partly from keyword discovery
flags.detail: The curated series tickers (for example KXAAAGASM, KXPGATOUR, KXEMMYCACTO) come from the fee schedule. Other series are added when their live title, tags or category contains a keyword. Each matched series shows its reason on its topic page. A reviewer should check any unexpected series.

flags.title: Live numbers were not checked from the build sandbox
flags.detail: The sandbox network does not allow Kalshi hosts, so every live value on the site comes from the GitHub Actions run. Each table row links to the JSON it came from, and status.json lists any endpoint errors. Spot-check a few rows against the linked JSON after the first run.

flags.title: Third-party fee articles were not used
flags.detail: Several web articles repeat the fee formula and claim things like '~160 series charge maker fees'. The count was not verified against the official schedule, so no third-party claim is used anywhere on the site.

links.label: Kalshi Fee Schedule (PDF), the official source

flags.title: Kalshi Developer Agreement and terms were not read
flags.detail: The API docs link to the Developer Agreement, which governs API use and automated trading. It was not read in this session. Read it before enabling any automated trading against a real account.

links.label: Developer Agreement (linked from the docs welcome page)

flags.title: Repository README is malformed
flags.detail: README.md contained only '# Trade2---' with no description and no trailing newline. It has been rewritten to describe the project. Details: REPO_REVIEW.md.

flags.title: GitHub Pages was publishing the repo root, not a site
flags.detail: Pages was configured as a legacy build from main /, which has no index page. It is switched to a GitHub Actions build of the site folder. See the integration log in COORDINATION.md.
